Stolen cable costs you a week of production Strip the copper out of a substation overnight and the scrap value of what they carry off is a few hundred pounds. What it actually costs you is a stopped line, idle shifts, missed deliveries and contracts you cannot fulfil. Getting everything back online can take weeks. Shift change is an open window for an opportunist For twenty minutes at every changeover, two or three times a day, the gates are busy, everyone is moving, and nobody is really checking. It is when contractors turn up unannounced, and when people walk in behind a group. It is also the point at which your record of who is actually on site is least reliable. The site grew but the cameras did not move New storage goes up, a gate gets added because it saves a walk, vehicle routes change after the last extension. One sighting and the airfield stops It does not take a breach. If someone reports a drone near the approach, movements are suspended, aircraft are diverted and the cost climbs into millions before anyone has established whether there was a legitimate threat. Gatwick lost 33 hours and around 1000 flights in December 2018. Almost nothing else in the country can be shut down this easily, or cheaply. Passes need to be up to date and open the right doors An airport runs on passes held by airlines, handlers, retailers and contractors you do not employ, tens of thousands of them at a major hub. Someone with a legitimate reason to be airside reaches places no outsider could. Your access control system decides what a pass can actually open, and the two drift apart the moment somebody changes role. They expect the alarm to go off The people who target collections now arrive knowing an alarm will sound, and it does not stop them. They plan well ahead, come with the right tools, take what they came for and leave in a few minutes. At the Louvre in October 2025 the thieves were inside for about four minutes and the whole job took under eight. Fewer eyes in the building than there used to be Budgets have not kept pace with costs, and rooms that once had someone in them are now covered on a rota, or not at all. In Art Fund’s 2026 survey of museum directors, 69% named staffing and capacity as their main challenge and 36% had cut opening hours. Visitors notice, and so do the people working out how a place is run. Large crowds come with extra requirements Martyn’s Law received Royal Assent in April 2025 and commencement is expected around spring 2027. Museums and galleries are named in the Act.
